title: Frontend's contact-address page explains what selecting does; Design release 1 explains who the contact is and what they are responsible for

finding.frontend: Under the heading "Contact address for consignment" the page's only guidance is the fieldset hint "Selecting a contact copies their name and address into this notification." (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/contact/copy/copy.en.js:4, rendered at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/contact/template.njk:11-23). That sentence describes what the service does with the answer. It does not say who the contact is, what they are responsible for, or over what period — so a trader choosing between the addresses in front of them is given no basis for the choice.
finding.prototype: Design release 1 puts a paragraph directly under the heading: "This is the contact address of the person responsible for the consignment from when it enters Great Britain until authorities complete their checks." (app/views/contact-address-for-consignment.html:50-52). It defines the role and its window, and it is the same sentence Design release 1 uses to describe the Branch Address type when a trader saves one. Design release 1 says nothing anywhere about copying the name and address into the notification.
finding.difference: Replace the hint with Design release 1's sentence, as a paragraph under the heading rather than as a fieldset hint, so it reads as guidance about the question and not as a note about the control. One string in src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/contact/copy/copy.en.js:4 and its Welsh counterpart, and a move from the radios' `hint` slot to body copy in src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/contact/template.njk:11-23. What the frontend's current sentence records — that this party is stored as a copy rather than a reference, unlike consignor, consignee, importer and destination (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/addresses/parties.js:61-70) — is a fact about storage that Design release 1 does not put in front of the trader, and dropping it from the page loses nothing the trader can act on.
finding.falsifiedBy: Finding the sentence about the person responsible for the consignment, or anything equivalent, anywhere on the frontend's contact page. The captured DOM of fe-contact carries only the one hint sentence between the heading and the first radio.
finding.verification: Ran the falsifier: everything between the h1 and the first radio in capture/html/frontend/fe-contact.html is the single hint "Selecting a contact copies their name and address into this notification.", which is src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/contact/copy/copy.en.js:4 verbatim, rendered into the radios' hint slot at contact/template.njk:20. Counted the lines by hand on the requirements side: app/views/contact-address-for-consignment.html:50-52 is the intro paragraph, a sibling of the header div and not a fieldset hint, in a root view. Checked the secondary claim by grepping the prototype's app/ for the sentence — it appears in that root view and at app/data/address-book-address-types.js:38 as the Branch Address hint, the remaining hits being the other releases' copies of the same view, which are not this comparison's document. Checked the converse too: grep for "copies their name" across app/ returns nothing, so Design release 1 really does not say it anywhere. Opened evidence/frontend@76a864ba/page/fe-contact.png and evidence/prototype@491b3926/page/dr1-contact-address-for-consignment.png. Rubric 8 fired on the correction's crop note, not on the claim — see correction. CORRECT.
finding.correction: The claim stands. The note this slot carried about the crop was wrong and has been replaced. It said the sentence "sits above" the radio group and so would fall outside a crop anchored on contactAddress. It does not: the rendered DOM puts the hint inside the same .govuk-form-group as the fieldset, the legend and all thirteen radios (capture/html/frontend/fe-contact.html, the form group opening immediately before the fieldset and closing after the last radio), and .govuk-form-group is the first entry in the anchor resolver's crop-ancestor list (tim/src/parity/resolution.js:22-24). So a crop on contactAddress frames the heading, the sentence and the radios together, which is exactly the comparison this finding wants. I did not run the anchor tool — that is the parent's — so this is a reading of the DOM and the resolver's own list rather than an observed crop. Design release 1 names its radios contactAddressId, so that side has no matching field name and falls back to the whole page, which also shows the sentence.
